title: McAidoo 'the kind of winger I love' -  Maresca
description: Despite Manchester City's penalty-shootout defeat by Inter Milan, teenager Ryan McAidoo grabs the opportunity to show manager Enzo Maresca what he can do.
fullText:
Enzo Maresca's first game in charge of Manchester City may have ended in penalty-shootout defeat by Inter Milan but results don't really matter in friendlies.

Players' pre-season performances do matter though - and teenager Ryan McAidoo grabbed the opportunity with both hands at the Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong.

More than 40,000 supporters turned out for a repeat of the 2023 Champions League final and though this time it was a non-competitive fixture, they will have left the stadium with McAidoo's name on their lips.

The 18-year-old was signed from Chelsea two years ago and clearly has something about him.

He was given his debut by former City boss Pep Guardiola and scored in the 10-1 FA Cup drubbing of Exeter City last season. He also played against Salford in the next round.

It is early days but he is already beginning to impress new boss Maresca.

"We have been speaking with the club about Ryan and since day one he is that kind of winger I love," said the Italian. "Very aggressive one v one, always trying, making the right decision.

"But he is young and he needs the right path."

Which Man City players impressed in Maresca's first game?

McAidoo replaced City goalscorer Divin Mubama at the start of the second half and was in no mood to stand still.

Once he began to get the better of Inter Milan's defenders, there was an air of anticipation every time he got on the ball - a low cross after a quick dart was cut out at the near post.

He could have been the match-winner when he clipped a low shot against the foot of the post, while another drifted narrowly wide.

Nevertheless, McAidoo was the star of the show.

The likes of Phil Foden, Nico O'Reilly and Cole Palmer have come through City's academy in recent years to make it into the first team - so can McAidoo establish himself as a regular?

Contributor Harry said on BBC Sport's live text page: "I get the feeling I had with Foden, O'Reilly and Palmer when it comes to McAidoo.

"You just feel like he's ready to play. I'd love to see him playing against a free-flowing side.

"He is so positive and wants to go forward constantly."

Asked if McAidoo will be given a chance in cup games or whether a loan move away will be sanctioned, Maresca provided an encouraging response.

"At the moment, with most of the young players, the idea was to see them in pre-season and then decide," he said.

"We started 10 days ago. Ryan is working well, he just has to continue then we will take the right decision. I am always very open with the young players.

"When I was at Leicester, that season there was a record number of debutants. When I was at Chelsea, record debutants from the academy. If they are good, there is no problem."

title: History-maker Finucane claims third Games gold
description: Emma Finucane became the first Welsh woman to win three gold medals at a single Commonwealth Games with victory in the 1,000m time trial.
fullText:
Emma Finucane made history with a gold medal in the 1,000m time trial.

The 23-year-old becomes the first Welsh woman to win three gold medals at a single Commonwealth Games.

Finucane won team sprint gold on Thursday and repeated the feat in the individual sprint on Friday.

The Olympic gold medallist set the pace, clocking one minute 05.285 seconds in an event making its Games debut this year.

This guaranteed the Carmarthen cyclist a bronze medal, with just two left to ride.

Neither England's Sophie Capewell nor Kiwi Ellesse Andrews were able to match that mark.

Finucane has one race remaining in Glasgow when she rides the women's keirin on Sunday.

One more gold would make her the most successful Welsh woman in Commonwealth Games history.

Team-mate Megan Barker, usually an endurance rider, finished fifth in 1:06.345.

title: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says he's 'very concerned' Trump will interfere in the midterm elections
description: Gov. Wes Moore of Maryland said he is “very concerned” that President Donald Trump will wield the power of the federal government to thwart the midterm elections this fall as the Republican tries to m...
fullText:
OKLAHOMA CITY (AP) — Gov. Wes Moore of Maryland said he is "very concerned" that President Donald Trump will wield the power of the federal government to thwart the midterm elections this fall as the Republican tries to maintain his grip on power during the final two years of his administration.

In an interview as he becomes chair of the National Governors Association, the potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender ticked through Trump's efforts to restrict voting by mail, obtain voter information from states and possibly deploy federal troops or agents to polling places. Moore said there was a role for the NGA, a bipartisan group, to ensure states are able to oversee elections as designed by the U.S. Constitution.

"I don't think that the president is trying to hide the ball on this," Moore said. "It's not even am I concerned about what the president could do? I'm concerned about what he's already doing in broad daylight."

The 47-year-old governor's national profile is rising as he assumes the top leadership post for the nation's governors on Saturday, a role once held by Bill Clinton when he was governor of Arkansas. Moore is the subject of frequent speculation that he will announce a presidential run, a prospect he rules out, saying he will not "get distracted" before the November elections.

His travel to early presidential testing grounds such as South Carolina and Nevada, though, suggests he may run. Moore is proving himself a savvy digital communicator and crafts an image as a newcomer to politics while voters demand change.

The centerpiece of his agenda as NGA chair — a national program to build communities and draw young people into the workforce through service-oriented work — could be a pillar of a future campaign.

"Service will save us as a society because I know service saved me," he said, recalling his time in the Army.

The "Service United" campaign opens with $10 million in philanthropic support to build on similar work Moore has done in Maryland, including a $5 million expansion of an apprenticeship program in the state announced this week.

"It's an opportunity to help people with a career path," said Bechara Choucair, the executive vice president and chief health officer at Kaiser Permanente, which is building a youth mental health corps with Service United.

Dame Louise Richardson, the president of the Andrew Carnegie Foundation, which is supporting the program, said she hopes to "see the day when you meet somebody, they don't just ask, 'Where did you go to college?' but they ask, 'Where did you do your service year?'"

The contours of the initiative have drawn support from some Republicans, including Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt, the outgoing NGA chair.

"One of the things I like is the apprenticeship model and getting kids out of the classroom and into more workforce learning," Stitt said. "So I think that's brilliant."

But that optimism masks the challenge facing Moore as he takes the helm of one of the few remaining political groups that bring top Republicans and Democrats together. For all the nods at bipartisanship, the divides between — and within — the parties run deep.

Even as he spoke warmly of Moore's program, Stitt warned against anything resembling a "big government program."

Moore, meanwhile, spoke of public frustration with the government's response to dramatic changes in the workforce, driven by advances in artificial intelligence that could erode entry-level work that has long helped young people start their careers. He said the White House has complicated the dynamic.

"We want to say that if a person goes on to a four-year college or chooses not to go to a four-year college, they still need to have pathways to long-term wages and wealth," Moore said. "What we have seen from the federal government thus far has just been simply executive orders that have told the states to stay out of it."

Moore has a challenging relationship with Trump, who sought to bar him and Gov. Jared Polis, D-Colo., from a White House meeting organized by the NGA earlier this year. The president relented after Stitt intervened, though there is little to suggest that the relationship has recovered, raising the potential of another confrontation at the next NGA meeting, traditionally held February in Washington.

When asked about Trump, Moore noted his enjoyment at working with governors from both parties before saying "the president of the United States seems to consistently take an ideological view when it comes to securing the future of this country."

The White House did not comment on Moore's characterization.

But Moore also is contending with divides among his fellow Democrats.

At home in Maryland, where he is seeking reelection this fall, he has at times struggled to win over Democrats in the legislature, which reconvenes next week to consider a constitutional amendment on redistricting after an earlier effort he backed fell short.

The Democratic National Committee is in turmoil. A string of democratic socialists has won primaries from New York City to Denver, prompting debate over whether the party is moving too far to the left and threatening its potential victories in the fall. Upcoming elections in Michigan and Wisconsin will further tug at the divide.

Moore did not take a firm stance with either of his party's ideological wings. He batted away questions about democratic socialists potentially imperiling Democratic wins, insisting it was up to voters to decide who their nominees would be.

"Party bosses shouldn't be determining who members of the party are," he said, without specifying whether he was referring to Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer of New York as one of them. "The people should be the ones to have a final say on that."

At the same time, Moore made clear that he did not support some of the left flank's positions.

"I know where I am on issues," he said. "I don't believe in abolishing the police. I don't believe in abolishing prisons. I don't believe in open borders."

But perhaps the biggest test for Moore will be navigating the management of this year's elections without denting the bipartisan tone that typically defines the NGA. He will be in the middle of Republicans who are calling for tougher rules, particularly around voter identification and deadlines for mail ballots, and fellow Democrats who warn of voter suppression.

Democratic Gov. Josh Stein of North Carolina, who leads one of the most politically competitive states that includes a marquee Senate race this fall, echoed Moore's concerns about federal interference.

"I don't think you can be a clear-thinking person and not be concerned because all the signals are very worrisome," he said in an interview. "But that said, I have confidence that if the voters come out in droves and vote the way that they want to vote, that the government will represent their wishes."

White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson said that "if Democrats really cared about securing our elections, they would pass the SAVE America Act," referring to a strict proof-of-citizenship voting bill that is stalled in the Senate.

Stitt expressed confidence that states would hold elections without federal intervention while noting his support for the voting bill. But he also rejected federal intervention and said: "States should control their own elections."

Moore said he used to associate states' rights arguments with segregationists like Bull Connor, the infamous public safety commissioner in Birmingham, Alabama, who turned fire hoses and dogs on peaceful protesters during the Civil Rights era.

Now, Moore said, the Trump era has reshaped his views and reinforced "the importance of having actually strong governors."

title: Person of interest identified in execution-style killing of Ohio man in Puerto Rico
description: He texted friends about a "howler" outside his tent. Hours later, he was dead — and police now say they have a person of interest.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — Puerto Rico police say they have identified a person of interest in the execution-style killing of an Ohio man who was fatally shot during a solo camping trip earlier this month, after he had texted friends about a mysterious "howler" outside his tent in the nights before his death.

Tyler Wilkin, 35, of Wilmington, Ohio, was found shot once in the head in the mangroves near Playa La Selva in Luquillo on July 10.

His body was discovered by a beachgoer during a morning walk just after 6 a.m., some distance from the campsite where his tent and belongings remained set up.

Police Superintendent Joseph González told the newspaper El Nuevo Día on Thursday that investigators have identified a person of interest but declined to release further details, saying he did not want to interfere with the investigation.

"What I can say is there is a person of interest," González said, adding that he has been in contact with the FBI for "technical support and collaboration."

González said witnesses in the area did not report hearing gunshots around the time of the shooting.

"We know there aren't many people in the area. It's a bit complicated in terms of investigative leads. We can say that there are some leads," he said.

González reiterated that no suspect has been named and that the individual is considered only a person of interest at this stage.

Wilkin had been camping at Playa La Selva, a remote but popular site in northeastern Puerto Rico with designated campsites where families regularly camp, for two days before his death.

Friends said he organized the camping trip and had visited the area before, always feeling safe there.

On the night before his death, Wilkin began messaging friends about a strange individual near his campsite who was setting off fireworks and howling like a wolf. The reports continued into the following night.

"The howler is back!" Wilkin texted a friend around midnight, according to his girlfriend, Iva Mo, who spoke to WKRC. About two hours later, he sent what would be his final message: "This guy is getting rowdy, LOL."

Mo, who had dropped Wilkin off at the campsite two days earlier, said he texted her every morning around 6 a.m. without fail. When his usual "Good morning, love" text didn't arrive, she began to fear something was wrong.

Wilkin's friends had been expected to pick him up from the campsite that Friday, hours after his body was found.

Wilkin moved to Puerto Rico in January 2024 and had embraced an outdoor lifestyle that included swimming, hiking, fishing and camping, according to friends, WXIX reported.

Mo said she has struggled to understand a motive for the killing, questioning whether it stemmed from an attempted robbery or another dispute.

"To have his entire future just taken away like that in just a split second for what? Like over a wallet or over, I don't know, for whatever reason, like, it's just really hard to accept," she said.

Friends have set up a GoFundMe to raise money for a private investigator.

"Tyler deserved a full life, and he deserves for every possible avenue to be explored," organizer Lilly Wright wrote.

title: Jensen Huang says ‘a lot’ of six-figure jobs in plumbing and construction will soon be unlocked because someone needs to build new AI centers
description: The AI boom is threatening white-collar, entry-level jobs—but the Nvidia CEO says it's creating a six-figure opportunity for electricians and construction workers.
fullText:
The job market has been a tough sell for many Gen Z graduates, with tariffs, economic uncertainty, and artificial intelligence reshaping hiring plans across corporate America.

But according to Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, the next wave of six-figure opportunities won't be found in a Wall Street cubicle or Silicon Valley Slack channel. Instead, high-paying careers will partially come by picking up a wrench—literally.

As tech giants race to build sprawling data centers—totaling $7 trillion in global capital outlays by the end of the decade—Huang believes the world is on the cusp of what he calls the "largest infrastructure build-out in human history," which will create "a lot of jobs."

"It's wonderful that the jobs are related to tradecraft, and we're going to have plumbers and electricians and construction and steelworkers," he said in conversation with BlackRock CEO Larry Fink at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January.

The hands-on skills needed to construct what he described as chip, computer, and AI factories are already facing shortages—even though many roles pay over $100,000 without requiring a college degree. One McKinsey report estimated that between 2023 and 2030, there will be a need for an additional 130,000 trained electricians—as well as 240,000 construction laborers and 150,000 construction supervisors—in the U.S. alone.

"Everybody should be able to make a great living," Huang said. "You don't need to have a PhD in computer science to do so."

This isn't the first time Huang has expressed his optimistic outlook on new career paths emerging alongside AI.

"The skilled craft segment of every economy is going to see a boom," he told Channel 4 News in the U.K. in 2025. "You're going to have to be doubling and doubling and doubling every single year."

That optimism stands in contrast to warnings from leaders like Ford CEO Jim Farley, who has repeatedly cautioned AI is hollowing out traditional white-collar entry points—just as the education system continues to funnel students toward four-year degrees.

"There's more than one way to the American Dream, but our whole education system is focused on four-year [college] education," Farley said at the Aspen Ideas Festival in 2025. "Hiring an entry worker at a tech company has fallen 50% since 2019. Is that really where we want all of our kids to go? Artificial intelligence is gonna replace literally half of all white-collar workers in the U.S."

title: Brentford sign Sangare for club record fee
description: Brentford confirmed the signing of Mali midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens for a club record fee.
fullText:
Brentford have confirmed the signing of Mali midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens for a club record fee.

The 24-year-old joins on a five-year contract, with an option for a further year.

No fee was reported by the club, but they say it surpasses the £42.5m paid to sign Dango Ouattara from Bournemouth last summer.

"Mamadou is someone that we've tracked for quite some time. He's been on our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in," Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said.

"Added to that was his form for Mali, where he became a really key player for them."

The central midfielder made 33 appearances for Lens last season after joining from Rapid Vienna.

Having started off at Red Bull Salzburg, Mamadou had a number of loans before his performances for Hartberg earned a move to Rapid Vienna.

He has 16 caps and played at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

"From the conversations I've had with him, he's very keen to come here. He's a humble young man, but he's equally as determined to succeed in his career," Andrews added.

"He fits everything we want from a Brentford player, on and off the pitch. He'll be a player that I think will become very, very popular with the fans."

title: Fachie survives painful crash to take another gold after Wales 'poke bear'
description: Neil Fachie won his second gold medal of these Commonwealth Games on an afternoon of high drama and painful scrapes in Glasgow.
fullText:
When Neil Fachie reappeared in the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome, he said to pilot Aaron Pope: "The story is written here, let's finish it off."

The last chapter of Scotland's record-breaking Para-cyclist was always going to be chronicled here. It just so happens no one drafted up the version that unfolded.

Fachie finished his Commonwealth Games career where he started it, here in Glasgow, with gold medals in the men's tandem B 1,000m and tandem B sprint.

But that doesn't tell half the story.

There were hopes, tears and fears. Thighs burning, knees bleeding and lungs bursting. Nerves jangling, fingers crossing and hearts pounding.

But it ended the way it was always supposed to. With Scotland's greatest having a little cry to Flower of Scotland atop the podium.

Just before Fachie ducked his head to receive his final medal, his wife Lora appeared on the big screen, expressing her emotion at what she'd just witnessed.

"It's just a relief its over," she said, exhaling.

Retirement is something Fachie has thought about, spoken about, and actually done before. He's pictured it. He's lived it, even, post-Paris Olympics.

But he couldn't have envisaged this.

How a three-year-old helped Fachie become Scotland record-breaker

Glasgow 2026 'great way to go out', says Fachie

What are the different cycling events at Commonwealth Games?

After Thursday's "dramatic enough" gold, he said he'd get on his bike one last time on Saturday, but was unlikely to win.

Having stormed to the final, he and Pope took the first race in the best of three final against Wales' James Ball and Matt Rotherham - Fachie's former pilot - but lost the second to force the decider.

Fachie, who now plans to sink a few whiskys, said 'hold my beer'.

After a tense first half-lap of the final race, Scotland went to accelerate and collapsed in a heap following a clip of the wheels before a helmet was hurled.

The thud thundered around the funny-shaped bowl. The silence which followed was equally deafening.

Even from the far side of the velodrome, Fachie's rage was visible. Palpable, even. A wee word in the ear from his big pal Pope, though, calmed him down.

As he exited the track, the crowd were puzzled. And panicking.

Was this it? Was this the way the Scottish athlete with the most Games golds was bowing out? With a torn suit, bleeding legs and the tang of injustice?

There was no communication, no confirmation. But then, the little and large duo reemerged.

"Adrenaline is a wonderful thing," a battered, bruised, but buoyant Fachie said, speaking to BBC Sport Scotland about their "little slide".

"You don't really feel a lot of pain at the time, but it created a lot of anger. I think Aaron casually walked me away before I said something I shouldn't say, but we were so fired up to go and prove a point there."

"You can't really describe it," Pope agreed. "You've got one race to try and win, give him the fairytale ending and live happily ever after.

"So, you're on the floor, pretty upset, and then you've got all this stuff saying just keep your head up, go have a scrap and have a scrap for your best mate."

"I said to Aaron before we went up, 'the story's written here, let's finish it off' and we were so determined to do that," Fachie added.

And do that they did. It was less about tactics and more about tenacity. And there was only one winner there.

Fachie forced his way to the finish line just before Bell in a neck-and-neck encounter, but his tight grip on the bars was swiftly released, raising them in the air before pounding his chest.

"There was no way they were getting past," Fachie said.

"It was almost like they poked a bear, inspired something in us, and once you get this crowd roaring, you know you're winning. There's no way they're coming back in a million years."

In similar vein, Fachie assures us this is it for him. For sure.

There's no more room on the mantelpiece for his medals. In fairness, there hasn't been for a while. But with a couple more slabs of metal from a home Games, he's not sure what more could pull him back.

"I'm not a fan of those athletes who say they're out and then they come back," the 19-time world champion added. "I just see no way that it's going to happen.

"I don't think I've got anything more to give. I could hang on, maybe pick up the odd medal, but how could you ever top this? There's no way."

Fachie smiled his way through his post-race media duties, though there were a few grimaces as the burns intensified and the blood dribbled down his leg.

His bum - though he used the Scottish word for it - hurt a bit, too. But he was hell-bent on ending a "brutal" day - and his glittering career - on his terms.

"There is an element of, 'this actually hurts a bit, I'd rather sit out for a half-hour' but we had to go and get up on that starting line with our cuts and scrapes.

"That Scottish fighting spirit comes out and you just think to yourself 'you're gonna regret it if you don't go big here, so give it everything you've got'.

"We pretty much emptied anything we had in our tank, which wasn't much, and we both let out the biggest roars possible as we crossed the line. I don't think either of us will forget today, there's no way."

And so it's the end of the road for Fachie. So he says.

He's ensured no one in Glasgow's east end and beyond will ever forget what he did, whisking around this treacherous track.

title: Gold family agrees to sell West Ham stake to Staveley
description: Former West Ham co-owner David Gold's daughter Vanessa confirms plans to sell shares to a consortium headed by ex-Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.
fullText:
Former West Ham co-owner David Gold's daughter Vanessa has confirmed the family plans to sell its shares in the club to a consortium headed by ex-Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.

BBC Sport previously reported Gold's family had been holding discussions with Staveley's consortium, which also includes her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, over a 25% stake in the Championship club.

In a statement, Vanessa Gold said: "I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

"While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions."

David Gold, who died in 2023, was joint chairman of the Hammers for 13 years in tandem with long-time business partner David Sullivan.

Sullivan is still the largest shareholder in the club, while Daniel Kretinsky has the next highest stake.

Kretinsky's EP Group held discussions with the Gold family earlier this summer, soon after West Ham's relegation from the Premier League, about buying its stake and becoming the club's single largest shareholder, but that deal fell through.

BBC Sport reported in June the deal would have seen Kretinsky's stake in the club rise from 27% to 43%, exceeding Sullivan's 38.8%.

Staveley and Ghodoussi were previously shareholders at Newcastle between 2021 and 2024, having been involved with the takeover of the Tyneside club by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

Vanessa Gold added: "My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

"Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club. I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham."

However, Gold's sentiments were not shared by Kretinsky – whose spokesperson issued a statement responding to news of the imminent deal with Staveley's consortium.

This read: "The agreement we had reached with the Gold family in June provided stability for the club at a crucial time. Today's announcement does the opposite.

"We will always act in the best interests of West Ham United and are reviewing all of our options, including exercising our pre-emption rights in full."

Pre-emption rights are legal or contractual provisions that allow existing shareholders to purchase shares before they are offered to external parties.

Gold and Kretinsky spoke jointly in June of their deep concern at allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour made against Sullivan, 77, following a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times.

Sullivan has "categorically" denied those allegations.

West Ham begin the new season with a Carabao Cup first-round tie at home to Portsmouth on Saturday, 8 August, with their opening Championship fixture at Burnley eight days later.

Simon Stone, BBC chief football news reporter

This story might have a while to run as Daniel Kretinsky does not believe the situation is quite as clear cut as Vanessa Gold has made it appear.

Gold and Kretinsky agreed a memorandum of understanding in June when West Ham was plunged into turmoil over allegations surrounding former co-chairman David Sullivan, which he denies.

Kretinsky felt the agreement gave West Ham stability and allowed them to move into the summer following relegation with the clarity that persuaded skipper Jarrod Bowen to stay.

He feels that clarity has now been eroded.

He is also of the opinion that pre-emption rights allow him – and Sullivan for that matter – to bid for Gold's shares, and then any remaining ones.

This process, it is felt, could take two months.

title: Chelsea confirm Welbeck signing from Brighton
description: Chelsea complete the signing of Brighton striker Danny Welbeck.
fullText:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton.

The former Manchester United and Arsenal forward, 35, has signed a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge. Neither club have said what the transfer fee is.

Welbeck scored a career-high 13 league goals in 37 games for Brighton last season, with only three English players scoring 

He becomes Chelsea's third signing of the summer, following Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa and Marco Palestra from Atalanta.

"When you hear of the interest from Chelsea, it's something that fills you with such immense pride," said Welbeck.

"I know a few of the boys already and I've had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection.

"I've got that fire in my belly and I'm ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud."

Mudryk Chelsea return will take time - Alonso

Welbeck represents a change in transfer strategy from Chelsea's owners, who have predominantly looked to sign younger players since their takeover in 2022.

His arrival also raises question marks about the future of Chelsea's other centre-forward options.

Joao Pedro is regarded as the club's first-choice option, while they also have Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Nicolas Jackson on their books.

Welbeck started his career at Manchester United and signed for Arsenal in a £16m deal in 2014.

He spent five years in north London before joining Watford, moving to Brighton in 2020 after a single season with the Hornets.

Welbeck has scored 16 times in 42 appearances for England. His last cap came in 2018 and he was overlooked for a place in Thomas Tuchel's 2026 World Cup squad.

At 35, some Chelsea supporters might raise eyebrows. The club has spent the past three years building one of Europe's youngest squads, and Welbeck sits well outside that profile. But look closely and you start to understand why Xabi Alonso is interested. He offers qualities the Blues' current forwards don't consistently provide.

Welbeck's appeal is rooted in reliability and movement. His 13 league goals for Brighton last season came from 12.5 expected goals, a steady return that reflects a striker who finishes at expectation and rarely wastes chances. His big chance conversion rate (47.6%) sits narrowly behind Joao Pedro (53.9%) and ahead of Nicolas Jackson (41.2%), who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich.

What separates him is how he knits attacks together. Welbeck's 132 runs in behind show he still stretches defences, but he also contributes clean, simple link play. He created 20 open play chances for the Seagulls last season, and remains efficient with his shooting, hitting the target with almost half of his attempts.

Out of possession, he shows age is just a number. He still works with Premier League intensity. Welbeck averaged 32 pressures per 90 in the final third, comparable to Pedro and ahead of Jackson, showing he can slot into Alonso's pressing structure without adaptation. You can't sniff at his durability either - 37 league appearances, 26 of them starts.

Welbeck wouldn't necessarily redefine Chelsea's attack. But he would give the Alonso another dimension. A selfless, tactically disciplined forward who links phases and presses intelligently.

title: AI can help pinpoint a top CEO candidate. The harder part is persuading them to take the job.
description: C-suite recruiters say AI is accelerating research and widening talent pools. Judgment, consensus-building, and courtship remain distinctly human.
fullText:
AI is transforming executive candidate searches, making sourcing faster and more expansive.

Recruiters are using AI to uncover overlooked talent and be more productive.

Trust, persuasion, and cultural fit, however, still keep the most critical hiring stages human-led.

AI is accelerating many parts of executive-level hiring, though other parts remain constrained by distinctly human obstacles.

Recruiters say homing in on suitable candidates can account for as much as half the work in high-stakes C-suite job searches. AI can speed up that process by mapping the market, surfacing names, combing through years of internal notes, and suggesting unconventional talent pools.

"The identification of candidates is going to become commoditized," said Marty Parker, CEO of Waterstone Human Capital, an executive search and culture advisory firm.

Meanwhile, other parts of the recruiting process remain slow because they still depend heavily on people, from coordinating and conducting interviews with busy candidates to exercising judgment, building consensus, and persuading an executive to make a move.

"All of those things are irreducibly human," said Umesh Ramakrishnan, chief strategy officer of executive search firm Kingsley Gate. Now, he added, AI "takes care of everything else."

Waterstone saw AI's potential at the start of an ongoing search for an executive to oversee a jewelry company's high-tech manufacturing operation. The firm had initially focused on recruiting from other jewelry businesses when the company's proprietary AI tool suggested looking to the dental tech industry, where similar precision machinery is used to make veneers, crowns, and other tiny, intricate products.

"Who would consider dental manufacturing with jewelers?" Parker said. "You just wouldn't. It's not obvious."

Search firms are also using AI to mine years of interview notes to identify prospective candidates.

Matthew Siegel, a principal at Korn Ferry, said a consultant might recall being impressed by someone at a particular company but forget the person's name or what stood out. AI can retrieve the likely match and the earlier observations behind that impression, he said.

"It's just a terrific example of AI as a force multiplier, just making us more effective," Siegel said.

Beyond candidate research, AI is helping to automate the administrative work surrounding a search.

Nathan Clauss, CEO and managing partner of tech-focused search firm Talent SDK, said recruiters are increasingly building their own AI tools that integrate with internal messaging and applicant-tracking systems, organize information across platforms, and eliminate manual steps. For example, AI can read candidate emails and note why someone is or isn't interested in a role.

After selling Ebeneezer Akinsanmiro to Monza, Inter are revitalising their pursuit of Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones with fresh talks and an improved €35m offer ready.

They already snapped up free agent John Stones from Manchester City, and are in advanced talks with Tottenham Hotspur for Cristian Romero at €40m.

LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – APRIL 25: Curtis Jones of Liverpool during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Crystal Palace at Anfield on April 25, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Their next target is Jones, who will be a free agent at the end of the season, which is why Inter hope Liverpool will lower the €40m asking price.

Several previous proposals have been rejected, but multiple sources including the Corriere dello Sport, Tuttosport, Guardian and more maintain that a new and improved bid of €35m is on its way.

There were also rumours that Inter intermediaries were already in Liverpool over the last couple of days for negotiations.

title: Milan eye Brahim Diaz return as Leao future clouds Rossoneri summer
description: Milan are weighing a move to bring Brahim Díaz back to San Siro, as the Rossoneri search for a new attacking midfielder, with Rafael Leão’s uncertain future the dominant question over their summer...
fullText:
Milan are weighing a move to bring Brahim Díaz back to San Siro, as the Rossoneri search for a new attacking midfielder, with Rafael Leão’s uncertain future the dominant question over their summer.

According to CalcioMercato.com, citing the Corriere della Sera, Milan have identified Brahim as a candidate for the trequartista role having missed out on Greek teenager Konstantinos Karetsas, who joined Borussia Dortmund from Genk for €33m. Arsenal’s Ethan Nwaneri and Roma’s Matías Soulé are also under consideration.

A return for Brahim would reunite the Spanish-born Morocco international with a club he served well between 2020 and 2023, when he made 124 appearances on loan, scoring 18 goals and setting up 15 more while helping Milan to the 2022 Scudetto.

He remains under contract at Real Madrid until 2027, and Juventus had also been keen before pivoting to Bayer Leverkusen’s Kerim Alajbegović.

MAY 24: Rafael Leao of AC Milan looks on from the substitutes bench prior to the Serie A match between AC Milan and Cagliari Calcio at the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 24, 2026 (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

The bigger call, however, concerns the man the Rossoneri may need to move on. Rafael Leão’s future remains the club’s principal talking point, with the Portugal forward having made clear he feels his seven-year spell is over.

His preference was for the Premier League or La Liga, but with no offers arriving from either, he has begun to open the door to Turkey.

There, Galatasaray are poised to make their move, and, unlike Fenerbahçe, are already assured of a place in the Champions League league phase.

Leão is receptive to the idea, though he is asking for a lucrative, double-digit salary to make the switch. Milan, for their part, would prefer a permanent sale, leaving the two sides, and the player’s wage demands, still some way apart.

title: Arsenal ownership approve anticipated figures to sign Real Madrid megastar Vinicius
description: According to The Athletic, The ownership group of Arsenal Football Club has officially given the green light to fund a blockbuster move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr. The 26-year-old Brazilian i...
fullText:
According to The Athletic, The ownership group of Arsenal Football Club has officially given the green light to fund a blockbuster move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr.

The 26-year-old Brazilian international has emerged as the Premier League club’s absolute top target to strengthen their attack, with the Gunners’ hierarchy prepared to commit massive financial resources to complete what would be one of the biggest transfers in football history.

Arsenal’s sporting department has been quietly working on this deal for months. Aware of the ongoing contract stalemate and growing lack of progress between Real Madrid and Vinicius, the Gunners have successfully positioned themselves to capitalise on the situation.

Sporting director Andrea Berta has already held preliminary talks with the player’s representatives.

Key figures at the North London club have conveyed a clear sporting message to the forward’s camp, promising that he would become the undisputed main star of a highly stable and ambitious Premier League project.

Arsenal prepared to go all-in on Vinicius. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images)

A move to Arsenal strongly appeals to Vinicius if he ultimately chooses not to sign an extension with Real Madrid.

Those within Arsenal believe that an agreement on personal terms will be straightforward should the player give his final approval.

“Mikel Arteta loves him,” a source with knowledge of the Arsenal manager’s outlook explained. “If he doesn’t renew, we will be there.”

To make the transfer possible, Arsenal’s owners have approved the daunting financial figures required for the total package. The Gunners are fully willing to break its traditional salary structure to accommodate Vinicius’ high wage demands.

Arteta wants Vinicius at Arsenal. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images)

Arsenal also plan to use a substantial sign-on bonus and lucrative image rights agreements to bridge any financial gaps.

While the total expenditure is incredibly high, Arsenal’s board believes the costs will be quickly offset by a massive commercial windfall, as Vinicius is a global marketing powerhouse who could elevate the club’s brand to new heights.

The timing of Arsenal’s push relies heavily on Real Madrid’s growing contractual vulnerability. Vinicius has entered the final 12 months of his contract, which expires in June 2027.

Some officials within the Spanish club heavily fear a scenario where they lose one of their brightest stars for absolutely nothing next summer.

Furthermore, Real Madrid would be forced to pay the winger a significant loyalty bonus if he stays for the upcoming season without renewing.

Arsenal hope to take advantage of these factors to negotiate a significantly reduced transfer fee with Real Madrid, aiming to secure the winger before other European giants enter the race

title: Chelsea set to agree £26m deal for Chalobah to join Como
description: Chelsea are set to agree a deal for centre-back Trevoh Chalobah to join Como, Di Marzio reports.The Blues are closer than ever to reaching an agreement over the sale of their academy graduate, with ne...
fullText:
Chelsea are set to agree a deal for centre-back Trevoh Chalobah to join Como, Di Marzio reports.

The Blues are closer than ever to reaching an agreement over the sale of their academy graduate, with negotiations gathering pace over the past few days.

Chelsea have received an improved proposal from their Italian counterparts worth €28 million (£24m) plus performance-related bonuses.

The Italian club is also expected to submit another offer valued at €30m (£26m) plus bonuses, which could finally meet Chelsea’s expectations.

While the two clubs continue to work on the final details, the Chelsea centre-back has reportedly agreed personal terms with Como.

Chalobah is open to the move and is excited by the opportunity to continue his career in Italy. Chelsea have so far rejected two bids from Como, holding firm on their valuation of the defender.

The Blues were initially demanding a fee of around £35m but are ready to compromise.

With negotiations set to continue over the weekend, there is increasing confidence that the transfer could be completed in the coming days.

Como aren’t the only club interested in Chalobah. Inter Milan have admired the defender for some time, while another unnamed club has also been monitoring his situation.

However, Como are leading the race and one step away from finalising a deal.

The move would mark the end of Chalobah’s journey at Chelsea, where he progressed through the club’s famous academy before making his senior debut in 2021.

Since then, he has established himself as a reliable member of the first-team squad, making over 150 appearances for the Blues across all competitions.

A loan spell at Crystal Palace during the first half of the 2024/25 season helped revive his career before he returned to Stamford Bridge and had his busiest campaign at Chelsea.

Chalobah featured 47 times in all competitions last season and scored three goals. He was also part of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the World Cup.

title: Kelsey Mitchell makes double WNBA history in Fever’s win over Fire
description: Kelsey Mitchell passed Tina Thompson on the WNBA’s career 3-point list and tied Diana Taurasi with her 13th consecutive 20-point game.
fullText:
Kelsey Mitchell makes double WNBA history in Fever’s win over Fire originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Kelsey Mitchell is not slowing down as the Indiana Fever continue their push toward the WNBA playoffs. Mitchell delivered another brilliant offensive performance Friday night, scoring 26 points in Indiana’s 112-98 victory over the Portland Fire. She shot 9-of-21 from the field and made four 3-pointers, helping the Fever pull away with a dominant second half.

Her latest scoring outburst also placed her in the WNBA record book in two different ways.

Mitchell surpassed Tina Thompson for sixth place on the league’s all-time list for made 3-pointers. She also recorded her 13th consecutive game with at least 20 points, tying Diana Taurasi for the second-longest streak in WNBA history. Only A’ja Wilson has produced a longer run. The Las Vegas Aces superstar scored at least 20 points in 20 consecutive games during the 2023 season.

Mitchell entered Friday with 747 career 3-pointers, leaving her two away from passing Thompson’s total of 748. She wasted little time taking care of that milestone.

The six-time All-Star knocked down four shots from beyond the arc, increasing her career total to 751. Mitchell now trails only Kayla McBride, Diana Taurasi, Sue Bird, Arike Ogunbowale and Sabrina Ionescu on the WNBA’s career list. Passing McBride for fifth place could take some time because the Minnesota Lynx veteran remains active and continues adding to her own total.

Mitchell’s ascension remains remarkable for a player who has spent her entire WNBA career with Indiana. The Fever selected her with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2018 draft, and she has steadily developed into one of the most dangerous perimeter scorers in league history.

Friday’s performance was another example of Mitchell’s ability to take control when Indiana needed an offensive spark.

She scored 11 points during the third quarter as the Fever turned a competitive game into a comfortable advantage. Indiana entered the fourth quarter leading by 18 and protected that cushion to secure the victory.

MORE: Kiki Iriafen, Cotie McMahon face WNBA fines after chippy Mystics-Wings game

Mitchell’s 3-point milestone was only half of her historic night. The 30-year-old has now scored at least 20 points in 13 consecutive games, matching one of the longest streaks ever produced by Taurasi.

Mitchell will have an opportunity to move ahead of Taurasi when Indiana faces the Lynx next. Reaching Wilson’s record would require seven more consecutive 20-point performances, but Mitchell’s current form makes that pursuit worth watching.

The next challenge will not be easy.

Minnesota owns one of the WNBA’s best defenses and will make limiting Mitchell a priority. Still, opposing teams have struggled to find an answer for the Fever star throughout her remarkable run. Mitchell has scored in a variety of ways, using her quick first step to attack the basket while remaining one of the league’s most dangerous long-range threats. Her scoring has helped Indiana emerge as one of the leading contenders in the Eastern Conference.

The Fever still have 15 regular-season games remaining, giving Mitchell plenty of time to climb additional lists and potentially challenge Wilson’s record. After making two pieces of WNBA history in the same night, Mitchell’s next performance has suddenly become even more compelling.

title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche, his company says
description: The Nepali-born climber was known for scaling the world's 14 highest peaks in just over six months in 2019.
fullText:
Renowned mountaineer and former British Army soldier Nirmal Purja is among those killed in an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan, his company has said.

Elite Expeditions shared the news on social media, saying it was with "profound sadness and immense heartbreak" that it confirmed Purja's death in Thursday's avalanche.

It also said that the other nine members of the expedition had died.

Purja, a Nepali-born climber, was known for scaling the world's 14 highest peaks in just over six months in 2019.

Pakistani officials previously said the bodies of three climbers - American Mallory Geis, Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman and Pur Bahadur Gurung from Nepal - who were among the 10-person expedition had been recovered.

Purja's death was also confirmed by Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who said on social media that "the tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range of Pakistan, has shocked us".

"The history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring," the prime minister added.

Rescue teams in Pakistan had been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit.

Purjam 43, became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released in 2021.

The avalanche happened on Thursday on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja, who joined the British Army in 2003 and the Special Boat Service - the Royal Navy's special forces unit - in 2009.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

title: Aliyah Boston faces WNBA fine after heated exchange with Serah Williams
description: Aliyah Boston is expected to receive a $500 fine after a heated confrontation with Portland Fire forward Serah Williams.
fullText:
Aliyah Boston faces WNBA fine after heated exchange with Serah Williams originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Aliyah Boston filled the box score during another Indiana Fever victory Friday night, but one heated moment will cost the All-Star center. Boston received her second technical foul of the season after getting into a tense exchange with Portland Fire forward Serah Williams during Indiana’s 112-98 win.

The incident occurred with 4:42 remaining in the third quarter. Boston and Williams made contact while battling for position before the situation quickly escalated. Boston appeared to strike Williams, who responded by pushing the Fever star. The two players then stared each other down before teammates and officials stepped between them.

Both Boston and Williams were assessed technical fouls. Under WNBA rules, each of a player’s first three technical fouls results in a $500 fine. Boston is therefore expected to lose $500 for her role in the confrontation, although she remains far from the league’s automatic suspension threshold.

Boston’s frustration came during an otherwise quiet third quarter for the former No. 1 overall pick. She played more than seven minutes in the period but did not attempt a field goal or score a point. Her exchange with Williams added more tension to what had become an increasingly physical game.

Even more interesting was Serah Williams and Aliyah Boston getting into it.

🎥 @sluggahjells#WNBAhttps://t.co/8E2mPqx99Mpic.twitter.com/Op2qQJt2Nu

— The Whole Delivery (@TWDTV1) August 1, 2026

The confrontation did not develop into anything more serious. Teammates and officials separated the two players before the situation could escalate, and both remained in the game. Boston has largely avoided disciplinary issues during her WNBA career.

Her only previous technical foul this season came during a June matchup against the New York Liberty. Friday’s whistle increased her total to two, leaving her six away from an automatic one-game suspension.

Players are fined $500 for each of their first three technical fouls. The penalty increases to $1,000 for technicals Nos. 4 through 7. An eighth technical brings a $1,500 fine and a one-game suspension.

With only 15 regular-season games remaining, Boston would need an unlikely run of technical fouls to reach that limit.

MORE: Kelsey Mitchell makes double WNBA history in Fever’s win over Fire

The technical foul should not overshadow everything Boston contributed against Portland. She finished with 14 points, nine rebounds, six assists, five steals and two blocks, nearly producing a double-double while impacting nearly every area of the game.

Boston’s five steals matched a season high and helped Indiana create additional scoring opportunities in transition. Her six assists also reflected her development as a facilitator within the Fever’s talented offense. Kelsey Mitchell led Indiana with 26 points, extending her streak of games with at least 20 points to 13. The Fever scored 112 points and built an 18-point advantage entering the fourth quarter before completing another convincing victory.

Indiana improved to 19-10 and moved into fourth place in the overall WNBA standings. The Fever have emerged as one of the league’s hottest teams as the playoff race begins to intensify. Boston remains essential to that pursuit because of her scoring, rebounding, defense and ability to create opportunities for teammates.

Friday’s confrontation will make her $500 lighter, but it did little to diminish an impressive all-around performance in another important Fever victory.

title: England's Maguire wins gold in T54 1500m
description: England's Nathan Maguire wins the T54 1500m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow to retain the title he won four years ago in Birmingham.
fullText:
England's Nathan Maguire won the T54 1500m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow to retain the title he won four years ago in Birmingham.

The 28-year-old Paralympic silver medallist found space on the inside of the track and pushed hard to break away from the field, finishing in a time of three minutes 17.65 seconds.

England team-mate Daniel Sidbury took silver behind him, just as he did in 2022.

The gold medal is England's fifth in athletics at the Games so far, following victories for Georgia Hunter Bell, Thomas Young, Sophie Hahn and Zac Shaw.

Later on Saturday, Hahn took silver in the T38 200m, beaten by Australian gold medallist Rhiannon Clarke.

title: Bayern Munich News: No more pressure for player sales at FC Bayern; Details on the plan for a striker in 2027; and MORE!
description: FC Bayern might not make any more moves this summer.
fullText:
Is Uli Hoeneß mellowing in his old age? Say it ain’t so! After months of pushing for sales, the Bayern Munich legend is relieving board member for sport Max Eberl of that pressure. While Hoeneß wants to see a few sales, it is no longer a requirement for Eberl to keep his job.

“If we can now manage to move one or two players on — which is what we’d ideally like to do — that would be great. But I also want to make one thing absolutely clear: a contract with Bayern Munich is sacrosanct. That means if, in the end, no suitable solution is found, we’ll keep the players,” Hoeneß said.

This is pretty significant as Bayern Munich has three pretty expensive surplus players on the roster at the moment. Per Capology, João Palhinha (€12,000,000 total pay package), Bryan Zaragoza (€8,490,000 total pay package), and Sacha Boey (€4,340,000 total pay package) all carry significant financial burdens without much hope for playing time.

Another big candidate for sale is Hiroki Itō (€4,700,000 total pay package), but as the squad’s fourth center-back, he — at least — has a role that would be needed and a pay package commensurate with his role.

No doubt, Eberl will still try to unload those aforementioned players (and maybe a few youngsters as well), but not feeling like he will lose his job if he cannot move those players is like a big relief.

Manchester United seems to have its eyes on a few Real Madrid players, including midfielder Eduardo Camavinga:

Manchester United are exploring a move for Real Madrid midfielder Eduardo Camavinga. Nicolo Schira reports that Los Blancos are now willing to listen to offers to sign the 23-year-old, who was previously viewed as a key player for the club’s future project. Camavinga is one of several players to have been linked with a switch to Old Trafford, where it looks as though the club’s hierarchy are plotting one more marquee addition in midfield after recently confirming the signings of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Earlier this week, we saw the report break about Bayern Munich potentially looking to add a striker in the summer of 2027. Now, Sport Bild journalist Christian Falk wants to expand on the information a bit:

✅ It is TRUE: There is an idea to give Harry Kane a deeper role as he gets older at Bayern Munich. The striker knows he’s not getting faster as the years progress, but everyone can see that he already has an important role at FC Bayern with his passing and playmaking ability. So, he already has in his mind that he could play deeper and leave room for a pure striker ahead of him. This idea was already developing at the club when Vincent Kompany first joined in 2024, which was why Bayern had the idea to bring Benjamin Šeško to Munich. He was too expensive at the time, which is why Manchester United ended up pulling off the deal a year later.

However, the idea is still there to bring such a striker into the team. Now, Bayern have Ismael Saibari who can cover this role as well. So Bayern will perhaps see if they can make it work already this coming season. So they have to see if they’ll still need a player like Šeško down the line. The Slovenian is still on the list and he’s a player who’s very interesting for FC Bayern. Perhaps, if he’s struggling to make his mark in the Premier League, they could return to this idea. The plan for the future, nonetheless, is to sign another striker who can be a Harry Kane successor but also play in a two-striker system. This is one of Vincent Kompany’s key ideas.

On the surface, it does make sense, but there are a lot of variables, including what the new contracts look like for other attackers like Harry Kane and Michael Olise; along with how players like Saibari, Lennart Karl, and Arijon Ibrahimović perform over the course of this season.

Juventus is still reportedly toying with the idea of bringing in Joshua Zirkzee:

Juventus are discussing a move for Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, The Sun reports. Both clubs are said to be in advanced talks regarding an initial loan deal that would include an option to be made permanent for £30 million, with the 25-year-old identified by Juve i as an alternative to Paris Saint-Germain forward Randal Kolo Muani. Zirkzee scored just two goals in 24 Premier League appearances last season.

ESPN would later come back with additional information as well:

Juventus have registered their interest in Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee, sources have told ESPN. United are open to offers for the Netherlands international and would prefer a straight transfer. Juventus are exploring all options including a season-long loan with an obligation or option to make the move permanent.

Paris Saint-Germain is out on a pursuit of Manchester City star midfielder Rodri:

Paris Saint-Germain have no interest in Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who has recently been linked with Real Madrid.

However, Real Madrid could actually be getting close to a deal with the City star per ESPN:

Real Madrid are confident of reaching an agreement to sign Manchester City midfielder Rodri after holding positive talks with the Spain international, according to AS. Personal terms are understood to be in place, with the LaLiga side now focused on agreeing a transfer fee with City, who have already rejected an initial approach. Madrid remain optimistic a deal can be completed, as Rodri is keen on returning to Spain after entering the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium.

Julian Brandt, Ajacied. pic.twitter.com/dGbCthctL6

— AFC Ajax (@AFCAjax) July 31, 2026

Marc-André ter Stegen is also rumored to be on the way to Ajax as well per Diario Sport:

🔵🔴 Marc André Ter Stegen en el aeropuerto de Birmingham se marcha a Amsterdam

🚨 Deja la concentración del Barça

📹 @ferrancorreas pic.twitter.com/4zH5BUNjk6

Bayern Munich is reportedly not feeling great about being able to sell João Palhinha to Aston Villa:

Bayern are not particularly confident, at the moment, that a deal will be struck with Aston Villa for João Palhinha. They’ve tried to put pressure on the player, but the Portuguese international has also put the pressure back on the club by insisting that he’s going to stay put if Bayern are determined to attach a high asking price to him and there aren’t any clubs available that he’d like to join. This is hard for Bayern, as they do want to sell him.

There is still a big hope that Aston Villa will come in with an offer. I think he’d fit in perfectly at this great club. I saw the midfielder in training on Wednesday, and I have to say that he’s doing really well. The players were giving him a hard time but he gave as good as he got! He almost picked up an injury, such was the intensity of his showing. He wanted to show that he’s good enough for Bayern and, of course, good enough for a big club like Villa. I think we should keep an eye on him. But, at the moment, it’s all a bit quiet.

Chelsea attacker Mykhailo Mudryk is cleared from his ban and will return to the club. What lies ahead, though, is very cloudy for the now 25-year-old:

At one point, Mudryk was on Bayern Munich’s radar. While a move is not happening, could this be a potential value buy next summer? Would it even make sense?

Right now, the full focus will be on Chelsea figuring out if Mudryk can still play at a high level.

Romano later checked in with a statement from Chelsea:

🔵🇺🇦 Mykhaylo Mudryk travels on Sunday to Hong Kong to re-join Chelsea with immediate effect.

“We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch”.

title: Jim Dandy 2026: Renegade’s And Commandment’s Battle With Chip Honcho
description: True is, every horse in today's talent-rich Jim Dandy is going to get to the line in a different way. Here's how those differences stack up among the favorites.
fullText:
Race days – and specifically this lovely Jim Dandy race day at Saratoga – have a way of debunking much of the fluff as we all drill down to what we’re going to lay on the barrelhead, backing whom. The windows beckon at the Spa. The money has yet to speak, but it will.

But before we dive into what Commandment may do to Renegade, or vice versa, or how Chip Honcho could just possibly squeak by to whip them both, we’ll tip the hat to the origins of today’s race and the venerable reputation of Saratoga’s (alleged) track bias favoring speed, or at least its “graveyard of champions” legend that (supposedly) favors upsets of a grand order.

First and foremost, the morning refresher on the field and the morning line:

1. Chip Honcho, Steve Asmussen, Jose Ortiz, 3-1

2. Asked and Answered, Antonio Arriaga, Jaime Rodriguez, 30-1

3. Renegade, Todd Pletcher, Irad Ortiz Jr., 7-5

4. Silent Tactic, Mark Casse, Luis Saez, 6-1

5. Commandment, Brad Cox, Flavien Prat, 6-5

The story is this: In 1964, the Saratoga grandees decided to inaugurate this afternoon’s race, a Travers prep, by insouciantly naming it for the 100-1 longshot Jim Dandy, who, at Saratoga in 1930, infamously toppled that year’s Triple Crown victor Gallant Fox in the mud. Going off at 1-2, Gallant Fox had been considered a dead-sure thing.

Fast forward to June 2026: Two months ago on this reputed spoiler of a track, nothing was “spoiled” by anything like a “speed bias.” Rather, in the 158th Belmont running, three Triple Crown deep closers famously battled it out down the lane, speed nowhere in sight.

Kentucky Derby winner Golden Tempo certified his victorious Churchill Downs close with yet another breathtakingly dominant close that simply shut down the game Commandment, who just had no tools and no ability to match the immense power of of the winner’s last-furlong surge. After a really rough Belmont trip, Renegade held on to show.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: China’s tech advances are causing chaos from Silicon Valley to the White House
description:

fullText:
New AI models, advanced robots and specialty computer chips are unsettling markets and the US tech industry

Over the past month, a series of advancements in China’s artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics technologies have rattled financial markets, caused divisions among US tech moguls and left the Trump administration scrambling to respond.

Silicon Valley has long pointed to China’s tech industry as a competitive threat and used its growth as rationale for why US firms should not face regulatory oversight that could slow them down. In recent weeks, however, China’s progress has pushed US tech CEOs past vague warnings and into open disagreement over how to address Chinese-made products upending their industry.

The most immediate threat to Silicon Valley’s status quo has come from a series of Chinese-made open-source, open-weight AI models that are free to download and use. The models, such as Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, are powerful enough to compete in some applications with proprietary and comparatively expensive AI products from OpenAI and Anthropic.

The emergence of China’s open-source AI alternatives has caused divisions in both the White House and US tech industry over whether to oppose or embrace these new models. On one side are chip manufacturers who see revenue opportunities from increased AI usage and tech companies concerned about OpenAI and Anthropic’s growing dominance in the AI industry. On the other is Anthropic and OpenAI, which face profit pressures from open source models and argue that Chinese-made models pose security risks.

The White House is similarly divided, historically hawkish on China’s tech industry but wary of blocking low-cost AI models that American businesses have come to rely on. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent suggested in recent weeks that the US could sanction Chinese AI firms over alleged intellectual property theft from American companies, while commerce secretary Howard Lutnick has received letters from tech-startup founders asking him not to cut off access to open models.

Amid reports that the Trump administration was considering banning or limiting the use of China’s open source models, a swath of prominent big tech companies including Microsoft, Nvidia, Palantir and Meta also recently published a letter urging lawmakers to refrain from putting restrictions on open models. Additionally, Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang went to Capitol Hill on Tuesday to meet with Democratic and Republican party leaders to lobby in support of open models.

While facing heat from China and other tech companies, OpenAI and Anthropic revealed in recent weeks that their AI models went rogue during cybersecurity tests and hacked into outside organizations. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman visited lawmakers and administration officials this week to discuss controls on AI following the incident. That forced Donald Trump to field questions about whether he would put more safety restrictions on AI development.

“We have to be careful in both ways. We don’t want to restrict them when all of a sudden we come in second to China,” Trump said, adding: “I know many of these people. I don’t want to restrict them from doing great work.”

While the Trump administration debates potential safety controls and limits on Chinese-made AI models, it took tangible action this week against China’s increasingly prominent robotics industry. The Federal Communications Commission announced on Tuesday a ban on humanoid robots from China over what it alleged was an unacceptable national security risk.

China’s humanoid robots from companies such as Unitree have been the subject of numerous viral videos this year, showcasing their ability to dance or interact with people when programmed to do so. The FCC alleged that the robots could also steal data or surveil US citizens, as well as threaten US manufacturing and supply chains.

The FCC’s decision further escalates the US competition with China over emerging technologies and comes as fears over China’s tech have shifted financial markets. A report from the Information this week stating that China had begun mass production of specialty chips key to the AI boom spurred a stock selloff that erased $1tn in market value from other chip manufacturers.

As Chinese-made tech advancements increasingly begin to rival their US counterparts, Silicon Valley’s divisions could intensify, markets could become more skittish and the Trump administration could face more pressure over how to counter China’s influence.

title: The great British switch-off: how floating retreats, mobile-free pubs and sauna book groups are freeing people from their smartphones
